page: Vultr vx1-m-4c-32gb is a memory-optimized server configuration belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It is driven by an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz, providing 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Cache provisions include 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory capacity stands at 32.0 GB, delivering an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU allocation ratio. Local storage consists of a minimal 1 GB NVMe SSD volume, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address without discrete GPU acceleration.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core throughput and highly parallelized workloads. The instance achieves top-tier results in single-threaded tests, highlighted by a stress-ng score of 3621.37 and 39.66 GB/sec in gzip compression, complemented by strong Geekbench text processing scores. In contrast, multi-core benchmarks like Geekbench compilation (5150.0) and parallel bzip3 decompression register in the lower performance quartiles, reflecting the constraints of a four-thread execution topology. Memory bandwidth performs steadily in the median range, reaching 69.51 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads and 41.08 GB/sec on uncached writes.

The architecture reflects a clear hardware tradeoff: generous memory capacity paired with a small core count and minimal local disk space. For workloads bottlenecked by RAM rather than disk volume or raw parallel CPU throughput, the instance delivers favorable operational efficiency without paying for unused compute cores. However, storage-heavy architectures will require supplementary networked block volumes. The system is well matched for in-memory data stores like Redis (measuring over 8 million SET operations per second), memory-intensive caching tiers, text parsing pipelines, and memory-bound backend microservices.
description: Vultr vx1-m-4c-32gb is a memory-optimized virtual compute instance powered by an AMD EPYC processor based on the x86_64 architecture. Configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs spanning 2 physical cores at 2.0 GHz, the instance provides 32.0 GB of system memory, establishing a generous 8 GB per vCPU ratio. Local storage is constrained to a 1 GB NVMe SSD, necessitating external block storage for data-heavy persistence. In benchmark testing, the instance shows top-tier single-threaded compute metrics, including high throughput in gzip compression and single-core stress-ng tests, alongside strong Geekbench text processing results. Conversely, multi-threaded tasks such as software compilation and parallel decompression show modest efficiency due to the low total core count. With zero GPUs and balanced memory bandwidth, the instance represents a cost-effective choice for memory-intensive tasks that require moderate processing, such as Redis caching layers, lightweight database read replicas, and memory-heavy backend API services.
